question: The list price of an article is Rs. 1200 and a discount of 15% is offered on the list price. The selling price of the article is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Discount%** = 15% ⇒ **Selling Price** = 85% of **List Price**.

SP = 1200 × (100 − 15) ÷ 100.

SP = 1200 × 85 ÷ 100 = 12 × 85.

SP = 1020.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1020.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **List Price (MP)** = Rs. 1200, **Discount Rate** = 15%.

**Formulas:** **Discount** = MP × Discount% | **SP** = MP − Discount.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/638758d9c08b2257c2c5f26020304f7002e8ad26c944f813ef4db9b1a816a51c.png] 

⇒ **Discount Amount** = 15% of 1200 = (15 ÷ 100) × 1200 = 180.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 1200 − 180 = 1020.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1020.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and List Price

The **List Price** is the price at which the article is listed for sale before any discount. It is functionally the same as the **Marked Price (MP)**.

Calculating SP with multiple discounts

If two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, SP = MP × (100 − d₁)/100 × (100 − d₂)/100.</p
